title: Opening a restaurant or snack in Mauritius
summary: The permits a food business needs and who issues each one: business registration, the Building and Land Use Permit, the trade fee, the Food Handler's Certificate, the fire certificate, the Tourism Authority's licence for restaurants, tables d'hôte and pubs, and the alcohol licence. With the fees that official pages state. Checked on 20 November 2026.
audience: Anyone planning to open a snack, a restaurant, a table d'hôte, a bakery or a food stall in Mauritius.

facts.label: Building and Land Use Permit: time for a decision
facts.detail: From the effective date of the application. 3 working days for a micro or small enterprise registered under the Small and Medium Enterprises Act 2017. No application fee.

facts.label: Food Handler's Certificate
facts.detail: For issue or renewal. Needed by every person who handles food for sale.

facts.label: Fire certificate
facts.value: Rs 1,000 for premises up to 1,000 m2
facts.detail: No application fee. Rs 1,000 more for each additional 1,000 m2 or part, up to Rs 25,000. Valid for 1 to 3 years.

facts.label: Tourist Enterprise Licence: application fee
facts.detail: The licence is valid for 12 months.

facts.label: Tourist Enterprise Licence fee for a restaurant
facts.value: Rs 5,000 up to 40 covers, Rs 10,000 above 40 covers
facts.detail: From the fee schedule the Tourism Authority publishes, a Government Notice of 2015. A pub pays Rs 10,000.

Alcohol licence for a restaurant, year 2026
facts.detail: Plus a processing fee of Rs 1,500 on the application. A pub pays Rs 8,000 and a table d'hôte Rs 4,000.

facts.detail: From the schedule of 2019 published by the business registry. A bakery pays Rs 3,000 and a pastry shop Rs 2,000.

sections.heading: What do you need to open a restaurant or snack?

blocks.text: Up to seven things, each from a different body: a business registration, a Building and Land Use Permit for the premises, a trade fee, a Food Handler's Certificate for everyone who touches food, a fire certificate, a Tourist Enterprise Licence if you open a restaurant, a table d'hôte or a pub, and an alcohol licence if you serve drink. This guide gives the steps and fees those bodies publish. It is not legal advice.

sections.heading: How do you register a food business?

blocks.text: The Food Act 2022 says no person may operate a food business without being registered under the Business Registration Act. A food business includes food services, catering and the sale of food. An individual registers with the Corporate and Business Registration Department on form BRF1 or online, and picks an activity from its list of trade codes. Some activities need an approval first: selling foodstuffs along the road, from a mobile unit or in markets and fairs needs the Ministry of Local Government, selling on the beach needs the Ministry of Tourism, and selling liquor needs the Mauritius Revenue Authority.

sections.heading: Do you need a Building and Land Use Permit?

blocks.text: Usually, yes. The City Council of Port Louis lists starting up a business and changing the use of a building among the cases that need one. Under the Local Government Act you apply to your municipal or district council through the National Electronic Licensing System. There is no application fee, though a council may charge a fee when it issues the permit. The council's committee must decide within 14 working days of the effective date of the application, or within 3 working days for a micro or small enterprise registered under the Small and Medium Enterprises Act 2017.

Get this permit early. The Tourism Authority asks for it, in the applicant's name, before it licenses a restaurant, and the Mauritius Revenue Authority asks for it with an alcohol licence application.

sections.heading: What is the trade fee for a food business?

blocks.text: Food trades are classified trades under the Local Government Act. The yearly fee goes to the council and is paid through the Registrar of Companies. It is first due 2 financial years after the business is registered, then every financial year. For 2026 to 2027 the first instalment is payable until 20 January 2027 and the second by 30 June 2027. A late payment carries a surcharge of 50 per cent.

items: Pastry shop or manufacturer: Rs 2,000, or Rs 1,000 for an individual.
Caterer without a canteen: Rs 2,000. Caterer or canteen employing fewer than 10 persons: Rs 3,000. Employing 10 or more: Rs 10,000.
Mobile seller of foodstuff and non-foodstuff, except on public beaches: Rs 1,500.

blocks.text: These amounts come from a schedule in the Government Notices of 2019 that the business registry still publishes as its list of trade fees. Our guide to licences and permits explains the relief the Act gives to small operators.

sections.heading: Who needs a Food Handler's Certificate, and what must the kitchen have?

blocks.text: Everyone engaged in selling, preparing, cooking, serving, packing, carrying or delivering food for sale must hold a valid certificate at all times, and you may not employ anyone who lacks one. The application goes to the Ministry of Health and Wellness. The certificate follows a medical examination by a Government Medical Officer and an approved course in food safety and hygiene. It costs Rs 300, lasts 3 years and is renewed at least 30 days before it expires, or a surcharge of 50 per cent applies. The fee provisions were set to start on 1 September 2025.

The Food Regulations 2024 also set the design of food premises. They must have potable water at all times, hand washing facilities within easy reach of food handlers, covered bins emptied at least daily, enough ventilation with a hood over every cooking point, and floors that drain and do not absorb grease. No sewage pipe, drain or inspection chamber may sit where food is prepared. Food may not be prepared in a room that opens directly onto a bedroom, bathroom or toilet.

sections.heading: How do you get a fire certificate?

blocks.text: You apply to the Mauritius Fire and Rescue Service on the National Electronic Licensing System, where every application and renewal has been filed since 13 September 2021. There is no application fee. The certificate costs Rs 1,000 for premises of up to 1,000 m2, and Rs 1,000 for each additional 1,000 m2 or part, up to Rs 25,000. The certificate is valid for 1 to 3 years, depending on the risk assessment, and the owner applies to renew it 60 days before it expires.

sections.heading: When do you need a Tourism Authority licence?

blocks.text: The Tourism Authority issues a Tourist Enterprise Licence to an establishment that provides services or goods to tourists for reward. Its list of tourist enterprises includes restaurants, tables d'hôte, pubs, nightclubs and private clubs. The licence is valid for 12 months. The restaurant checklist of 15 May 2025 asks for the business registration card, the title deed or lease, site and layout plans, the Building and Land Use Permit, the proposed menu and a certificate of character, with an application fee of Rs 1,500.

items: A restaurant needs at least a reception or bar area, a common dining area, a kitchen, a scullery separate from the kitchen, toilets and parking.
One parking slot is required for every 8 m2 of dining area.
A restaurant of more than 40 covers needs a generator or another back-up supply. All need water tanks, a first-aid kit and a fire extinguisher.
A table d'hôte serves local cuisine in the licensee's home, with a dining area of at least 1 m2 for each guest, and opens from 10.00 to 22.00.
A pub needs a floor area of at least 50 m2 and is authorised only in a shopping mall or a business or commercial area.

sections.heading: How do you get a licence to sell alcohol?

blocks.text: Nobody may sell liquor or alcoholic products without a licence from the Director-General of the Mauritius Revenue Authority. You file the form with a processing fee of Rs 1,500, which is not refunded. The documents include the Tourist Enterprise Licence for a restaurant, pub or table d'hôte, the Building and Land Use Permit, the business registration card and a recent certificate of character from the Director of Public Prosecutions. Officers visit the premises, and a licensing committee decides. The licence runs from the day you pay to 31 December. For 2026 a restaurant or a pub pays Rs 8,000 and a table d'hôte Rs 4,000.
A licensee may not sell alcohol to anyone under 18 and must keep to the authorised hours. Our guide to eating out lists them.

sections.heading: What extra rules apply to bakeries, food vehicles and street stalls?

items: Bakeries. Regulations in force since 11 April 2026 list the types of bread a baker may make and their maximum prices, such as Rs 3.90 for a 100 g maison loaf. Another type needs the council's approval. The bakery displays a notice of the type, weight and price of its bread and keeps a stamped scale for customers.
Food vehicles. The driver's cabin is sealed off from the food. The vehicle carries a sink with potable water, a wash-hand basin, refrigeration, a covered bin and a waste water tank.
Street stalls. The stall, cart, bicycle or tricycle must be designed or adapted for the food sold, and the food stays covered. A hawker needs an authorisation from the council.
Everyone. The price shown to a customer must include VAT.

Whether a restaurant pays a trade fee. The Twelfth Schedule to the Local Government Act names a restaurant without liquor or entertainment as a classified trade, but the fee list of 2019 read on the registry's site shows no fee for it.
Whether the trade fee amounts of 2019 have been amended. The registry publishes a scanned copy that had to be read as images.
Whether a small eating place that serves no alcohol and no tourists needs a Tourist Enterprise Licence. The Tourism Authority's pages do not say.
Whether the Tourist Enterprise Licence fees of 2015 are still in force. The Tourism Authority's file is named as its new operating fees, but the scan is of Government Notices 2015.
The fee each council charges when it issues a Building and Land Use Permit, and the documents its guide asks for.

How to book the medical examination and the course for the Food Handler's Certificate, and what the course costs. Whether a health clearance separate from the Food Handler's Certificate is needed before opening. The Tourism Authority's guidelines mention a health clearance, but no Ministry of Health page describing one was found.
